newsitem.title: USA: Florida home resales rise 1 percent in October.
newsitem.headline: Florida home resales rise 1 percent in October.

text.p: Florida sales of existing, single-family homes rose 1 percent in October, compared to October of last year, the Florida Association of Realtors said Monday.
Florida year to date resales rose by 7 percent over the first 10 months of last year, the association said.

The group attributed the gains to favorable interest rates. The average rate of a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage was 7.92 percent, down from September's average of 8.23 percent and slightly up from the 7.48 percent average in October 1995.
The median sales price rose to $87,500 in October, an increase of one percent over October of last year.

Florida's housing market remained strong despite a national slowdown. Nationwide, home sales fell by 1.5 percent in October, compared to September, and were down 2.5 percent over October of last year.

"Florida's image in the consumer's mind is a positive one," said Association President Cathy Whatley. "Good job opportunities, wonderful weather and friendly neighbors all add up to be great reasons to buy a home or a commercial investment."
The Sarasota-Bradenton Metropolitan Statistical Area saw a 20 percent jump over October of last year, partly due to flexible pricing that helped attract first-time buyers.
The Miami area remained a buyers market, with a 9,000-home inventory.
"But the market could not be more robust," said realtor Tom Byrne. "Sales are taking longer because buyers are looking at more homes to find that bargain."

Among major metropolitan areas, sales were up 12 percent in Fort Myers-Cape Coral, 32 percent in Fort Pierce-Port St. Lucie, 14 percent in Lakeland-Winter Haven, 20 percent in Melbourne-Titusville, 16 percent in Naples, 34 percent in Panama City, up 29 percent in Pensacola, up 21 percent in Punta Gorda, and up 17 percent in Tallahassee.
Sales were down 5 percent in Daytona Beach, down 29 percent in Fort Lauderdale, and down 18 percent in West Palm Beach.
